minorIssues.description: The setImmediate-deferred truncation check fires correctly on truncated envelopes but ALSO fires when a consumer iterates the for-await loop without consuming part bodies on a well-formed envelope. Reproducer: `for await (const part of parseMultipartRelated(res, ...)) { count++; }` (no `for await (const c of part.body)` drain) on a 1-part well-formed envelope yields part 0 then throws MultipartTruncatedError on the next iter.next(). This is because dicer's 'finish' depends on the per-part stream's buffered chunks being consumed, so dicerFinished stays false when the consumer ignores the body. Real-world callers MUST drain part bodies (the planner notes this is the FR-DR-A-029 contract), and every test in tests/ that uses the iterator drains bodies — so no test fails. But it is a behavioral regression from Sprint 2 (which had no truncation detection) for the no-drain pattern. Recommend a future sprint either: (a) document that body drain is mandatory in api.md, (b) detect this case and emit a friendlier 'parts not consumed' diagnostic, or (c) accept that body drain is implicit-mandatory and the spot-check pattern is unrealistic. Not a critical bug — production usage is always with body drain.

assumptionsReview.context: setImmediate-deferred truncation detection lets dicer's pipe-driven 'finish' tick land first on well-formed envelopes
assumptionsReview.choice: onSourceEnd schedules setImmediate; the callback checks dicerFinished + cleaned flags before pushing MultipartTruncatedError. Cleaned-flag short-circuit prevents pushing into a closed queue when cleanup runs before the setImmediate callback
assumptionsReview.rationale: The setImmediate boundary is the next-macrotask after process.nextTick — dicer's pipe-driven 'finish' uses process.nextTick chains, so setImmediate reliably runs AFTER dicer has had a chance to fire. Empirically verified by the test suite (T-001 + 12 other parse-multipart-related tests pass with this delay). Truncated envelopes leave dicerFinished=false at the setImmediate boundary; well-formed envelopes have dicerFinished=true by then. The only edge case where this misfires is when the consumer doesn't drain part bodies on a well-formed envelope — captured under minorIssues[]. Not a race window in normal use; not papering over a real bug.

assumptionsReview.context: allPartStreams Set as belt-and-suspenders alongside queue.drainPendingParts()
assumptionsReview.choice: Maintain a Set of every per-part Readable dicer emitted on 'part' (synchronous from dicer's emit). On cleanup, queue.drainPendingParts() destroys queued parts, then allPartStreams iterates and destroys any not-yet-destroyed remainder
assumptionsReview.rationale: This is NOT papering over a queue bug. The legitimate gap: dicer emits 'part' BEFORE the per-part stream's 'header' event fires. Only after 'header' does parseMultipartRelated push the StreamingMultipartPart into the queue. On synchronous source-error paths (T-068), the part stream may exist but never reach its 'header' event — so it's outside queue.drainPendingParts() coverage. The allPartStreams Set captures it at dicer-emit time. The Sprint 3 report's assumption #4 documents this clearly. Two test cases exercise both paths: the drain-on-finally test (parse-cleanup.test.ts:327-353) hits the queued-but-not-yielded path; T-068 (parse-cleanup.test.ts:112-153) hits the not-queued-yet path.

assumptionsReview.context: Per-part stream 'error' handler scope (Sprint 3 added handlers that previously crashed test workers under truncation)
assumptionsReview.choice: onPart attaches a partStream.on('error', ...) listener immediately at construction time. Pre-cleanup it routes errors to the queue via queue.signalError; post-cleanup it routes via logger.warn 'multipart: late part-stream error after generator close'
assumptionsReview.rationale: In scope for Sprint 3 — without this handler, dicer's per-part Readable can emit an unhandled 'error' event when the source is destroyed mid-part (e.g. during T-066 / T-068), which crashes the Node process. The brief explicitly calls out NFR-006 'battle-tested' hygiene; bridging per-part stream errors into the same observable path as dicer-level errors is exactly the hygiene gap. The handler shape mirrors the dicer-level discriminator (cleaned flag + summarizeError + identical logger event shape) — design consistency is preserved. The Sprint 3 report's assumption #3 acknowledges this added scope was needed to make T-066 / T-068 pass cleanly without process.on('uncaughtException') workarounds.

assumptionsReview.context: Patch Dicer.prototype.emit in tests/fixtures/dicer-activity.ts vs subclass-and-swap
assumptionsReview.choice: Patch Dicer.prototype.emit in place; restore() reverses
assumptionsReview.rationale: Subclass-and-swap can't work because production code's FR-DR-A-028 normalization resolves the constructor at module load time, so swapping the namespace AFTER imports doesn't affect already-resolved bindings. Prototype patching works regardless of which namespace slot the production code resolved (all Dicer instances share one prototype). Reversibility verified — every test uses afterEach(() => tracker.restore()). No leak across tests (verified by clean pnpm test runs).
